content.value_statement: Belgian bereavement administration involves multiple institutions and regional requirements. This guide helps an AI assistant draft roadmaps, notification letters, and paperwork checklists for review.
actual_capabilities: Guides drafting a day-by-day administrative roadmap for the first week after a death in Belgium.
Provides context for drafting notification letters to banks, insurers, and utility providers.
Identifies Flanders, Brussels, Wallonia, and place of death as considerations for inheritance declaration planning.
Frames questions about a MyMinfin Certificate of Heredity versus a notarial act.
Suggests administrative checklists covering Belgian authorities and utility sectors.
limitations: The package contains one public guide; original scripts, extension source, and templates are not included.
No executable deadline calculator, detailed decision rules, or service integrations are supplied.
The claimed June 2026 legal currency is not supported by cited legal sources in the guide.
Drafts require professional review, especially for debts, minor heirs, and complex estate liquidation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a family handover checklist
use_cases.description: Draft a first-week roadmap and institution checklist for a bereaved family to review with responsible professionals.

use_cases.title: Draft institution notifications
use_cases.description: Prepare bank, insurer, and utility notification drafts using placeholders for sensitive identifiers.

use_cases.title: Organize estate administration questions
use_cases.description: List regional filing questions and missing information before discussing inheritance paperwork with a notary or tax authority.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first-week checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a first-week Belgian bereavement checklist for [municipality] after a death on [date]. Ask for missing facts and flag legal requirements needing verification.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a bank notification
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a bank death notification for [bank] from [relationship]. Use placeholders for identifiers and ask the bank to confirm required documents and account procedures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare correspondence without exposing sensitive identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Plan regional deadline verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a filing timeline worksheet for [Belgian region], death on [date], and place of death [country]. List missing facts and require official deadline verification.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an estate review dossier
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a review dossier for [family circumstances], [Belgian region], and [place of death]. Include notification drafts, certificate questions, notary questions, and unresolved legal assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate multiple administrative documents for professional review.

output_examples.input: Draft a bank notification after a parent dies, without including real account details.
output_examples.output:

Please explain applicable account procedures and any available support for eligible survivors.

[sender name and contact details]

output_examples.input: Prepare inheritance filing questions for a Belgian resident who died abroad.
output: Confirm the relevant Belgian region and the date and country of death.
Ask the competent authority which declaration deadline applies to these circumstances.
Confirm required foreign documents, translations, and any legalization requirements.
Ask whether a Certificate of Heredity is sufficient or a notarial act is required.
Record the verified deadline, official source, and person responsible for filing.

best_practices: Provide the relevant Belgian region, date of death, place of death, and family circumstances before requesting a roadmap.
Use placeholders for national identifiers, account numbers, and other sensitive personal information.
Verify deadlines, certificate requirements, and survivor banking rules with official authorities or a qualified notary before acting.
anti_patterns: Treating generated deadlines or benefit amounts as verified legal advice.
Assuming this guide submits declarations, contacts institutions, or includes the original package tools.
Using general administrative drafts to settle complex estates without professional review.

faq.question: What is included in this package?
faq.answer: One SKILL.md public guide is included. Original scripts, extension source, and templates are not supplied.

faq.question: Which Belgian regions does the guide cover?
faq.answer: It discusses Flanders, Brussels, and Wallonia. Regional rules and filing locations still require official verification.

faq.question: Does it calculate legally reliable filing deadlines?
faq.answer: The guide claims deadline support but provides no executable calculator or detailed calculation rules. Confirm any proposed deadline with the competent authority.

faq.question: Can it help when the death occurred abroad?
faq.answer: The guide discusses deaths abroad and adjusted filing timelines. It does not include the separate module described in its promotional text.

faq.question: Does it replace a notary?
faq.answer: No. It supports administrative drafting and preparation, not formal estate liquidation or individualized legal advice.

faq.question: Does it submit documents or notify institutions?
faq.answer: No submission tools or institution integrations are included. Review drafts and send documents through the appropriate official channels.
